title.content: Let \(f\) be defined by \(f(x)=\sin x+\cos x\) and let \(g\) be defin…

expected_question.statement: Let \(f\) be defined by \(f(x)=\sin x+\cos x\) and let \(g\) be defined by \(g(u)=\sin u+\cos u\), for all real numbers \(x\) and \(u\). Then:

choices.content: \(f\) and \(g\) are exactly the same functions
If \(x\) and \(u\) are different numbers, \(f\) and \(g\) are different functions
Not enough information is given to determine if \(f\) and \(g\) are the same

feedback.content: Both \(f\) and \(g\) are given by the same rule and are defined on the same domain; therefore they are the same function.

title.content: Given two infinite decimals \(a=.3939393939\ldots\) and \(b=.67766777…

expected_question.statement: Given two infinite decimals \(a=.3939393939\ldots\) and \(b=.67766777666\ldots\), their sum \(a+b\):

choices.content: Is not defined because the sum of a rational and irrational number is not defined
Is not a number because not all infinite decimals are real numbers
Can be defined precisely by using successively better approximations
Is not a real number because the pattern may not be predictable indefinitely

feedback.content: Every infinite decimal represents a real number, apart from the familiar non-uniqueness involving repeating 9s and repeating 0s. The sum can therefore be defined precisely by successively better approximations.

title.content: Consider the function

expected_question.statement:

\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}

title.content: Suppose two linear functions \(f\) and \(g\) are shown below

expected_question.statement:
Suppose two linear functions \(f\) and \(g\) are shown below.

![Graph of two linear functions](asset:math-limits-015-graph)

Then \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to a}\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\) is:

feedback.content: By similar triangles, \(f(x)/6=(x-a)/(0-a)=g(x)/3\), so \(f(x)/g(x)=6/3=2\). Equivalently, the limit is the ratio of the slopes of \(f\) and \(g\).

images.alt_text: Two lines f and g through the point with horizontal coordinate a, with vertical intercept labels 6 and 3

cases.rationale: Figure géométrique indispensable et feedback comprenant deux méthodes.

title.content: A boat is drawn close to a dock by pulling in a rope, as shown

expected_question.statement:
A boat is drawn close to a dock by pulling in a rope, as shown.

![Boat, rope and dock](asset:math-related-rates-002-boat)

How is the rate at which the rope is pulled in related to the rate at which the boat approaches the dock?

choices.content: One is a constant multiple of the other
It depends on how close the boat is to the dock

feedback.content: Let \(z(t)\) be the rope length and \(x(t)\) the horizontal distance to the dock. From the Pythagorean theorem, differentiation gives \(z\,dz/dt=x\,dx/dt\), so the relationship depends on position.

images.alt_text: Boat connected by a rope to an elevated dock

title.content: The region between two concentric circles of radii \(r_1\) and \(r_2\…

expected_question.statement:
The region between two concentric circles of radii \(r_1\) and \(r_2\), with \(r_2>r_1\), is an annulus of area \(\pi(r_2^2-r_1^2)\).

![Annulus](asset:math-mvt-007-annulus)

Which statement is correct?

choices.content: The area can be approximated by rectangles, but no single rectangle necessarily has exactly the same area
The area cannot be approximated by rectangles because the circles are concentric
There is a radius \(r\) between \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) such that a rectangle of base \(r_2-r_1\) and height \(2\pi r\) has exactly the area of the annulus

feedback.content: By the mean value theorem, \((A_2-A_1)/(r_2-r_1)=2\pi r\) for some \(r\in(r_1,r_2)\). Hence \(A_2-A_1=2\pi r(r_2-r_1)\), exactly the area of the stated rectangle.

images.alt_text: Annulus between concentric circles of radii r1 and r2
